frontier.hypothesis: The insn that holds LUID 42 does not have to be `addiu a0,sp,0x10`. If the first argument's value is born as its own insn earlier in the block (a pointer local to the local struct, `S46C *ps = &s;` hoisted out of the loop, called as `func_80073728((s32)ps, 0)`), expand_call's move becomes `a0 = pseudo` - a separate insn that greg coalesces away - so the deciding ready list at clock 64 contains a different insn set and sched2 sees a different post-reload stream.
frontier.mechanism: calls.c:1880 always emits the hard-register move last, but WHAT that move copies is source-determined. A pseudo-to-hard-reg copy is a candidate for coalescing in local-alloc/greg, so the insn can vanish before sched2 while still having occupied LUID 42 during sched1 - the only route found so far that changes which insn wins the sched.c:2462 tie-break without touching the a2 expression.
frontier.next_probe: First read rejected/struct-via-pointer-local-scores-60.c and rejected/tu-local-struct-pointer-mixed-scores-10.c to confirm those measured the D_8009B2E0 object model rather than a pointer to the LOCAL struct s. Then build the `S46C *ps = &s;` form, require build_insns == 176, and capture the BB2_SCHED_DEBUG clock-64 window plus the sched2 RTL segment; the trace (which insn holds the top two LUIDs), not the score, is the signal.

frontier.hypothesis: sched1 cannot produce the target order, but sched2 runs on a renumbered post-reload stream; there may be a sched1 emission order, other than the target's own, whose sched2 output is the target order.
frontier.mechanism: sched2 recomputes INSN_LUID over the sched1-emitted chain, so its tie-break input is the sched1 OUTPUT order rather than the RTL birth order. s9 recorded sched2 as a no-op for the control because the control's emitted order is already a sched2 fixpoint; that says nothing about other sched1 orders. If some reachable sched1 order maps onto 240,242,205,211 under sched2, the calls.c:1880 LUID bound is bypassed entirely.
frontier.next_probe: Use tools/sched_solver to invert sched2 over the four-insn window: enumerate every pre-sched2 order whose sched2 output is 240,242,205,211, then intersect that set with the sched1 emission orders the s6 depth-1/depth-2 searches showed to be reachable. Bank the intersection - possibly empty, which would itself be a class kill with a sched.c predicate.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual may not be reachable by any change to the a2 expression at all; the remaining degree of freedom is which basic block the argument moves terminate. If the func_80073728 call sits at the end of a block whose successor differs (a chassis where one half is guarded, or the loop is restructured so the call is not in the same block as the struct stores), the sched1 window itself changes shape.
frontier.mechanism: schedule_block operates per basic block, and both the LUID numbering and the ready-list contents are block-local. Every form measured in ten sessions keeps both halves and both calls in one block; the s5b loop-chassis sweep varied the loop form but never the block boundaries inside the body.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate source forms that split the loop body into more than one basic block without changing the emitted instruction multiset (an `if` on an already-computed condition whose arms are both taken, a `continue` at the end of the first half), measure each with build_insns == 176 as the gate, and capture the SCHEDDBG window for any form whose block count changes.
